rows.notes: The cited document is a review article (Reviews of Geophysics) synthesising ground, proximal and satellite soil moisture sensing techniques, data resources, root-zone estimation methods and applications. It contains a few illustrative author-generated figures (e.g. Fig. 10 GPS-IR vs SMAP L4 comparison; Fig. 17 lab evaporation experiment; Fig. 25 SMAP L4 variability), but these are not studies of remote sensing delivering crop production outcomes; the agriculture section (9.2) and the root-zone SM section (7) only cite other work (e.g. Ines et al. 2013, Han et al. 2016, Chakrabarti et al. 2014) on irrigation scheduling and yield. No primary result of its own on the claimed effect.

Same review article; no own experiment, survey or validated model on remote-sensing soil moisture delivering climate-resilient agricultural or risk management. Sections 9.2-9.3 on agriculture, drought, floods and landslides summarise results of other studies (e.g. Louvet et al. 2015, Wanders et al. 2014, Segoni et al. 2018) and recommend integration of SSM products with soil hydraulic data for drought monitoring as future work; the SSM-to-RZSM gap discussed in the passage is treated in the review's section 7 and summary point 6 as a remaining challenge, not a demonstrated effect.
